Since finishing my favourite, L’Oréal lumi glotion, I wanted to try something new. This product is more of a gel than a lotion. It stays really wet and takes a while for it to dry down. It’s also less glowy than the glotion. 

Once this is done, I’ll go back to my glotion.

There's a $35 secret hiding in your makeup aisle. e.l.f.'s Halo Glow Liquid Filter and Charlotte Tilbury's Hollywood Flawless Filter share 16 ingredients — the same water-plus-squalane-plus-silicone glow skeleton that creates that lit-from-within finish. We checked both published ingredient lists (Ulta and Sephora, today) so you don't have to take TikTok's word for it.

The e.l.f. version leans more hydrating — hyaluronic acid, sunflower seed oil, calendula — with a touch more shimmer. The CT original is thinner, more blurring, more refined. Reviewers give the $15 version 4.3 stars across 24,300+ ratings, and it's 100% vegan and cruelty-free.

At $15 at Ulta versus $50 at Sephora, this is the dupe that started a genre. Save $35 — or buy three and still spend less than one CT.
